- We need to maintain technical documentation throughout the system lifecycle

- This is not about changing WHAT we research but HOW we engineer and document

The most cost-effective response is to treat logging and documentation as shared platform infrastructure—built once, reused across projects—so we do not multiply compliance headcount by the number of concurrent R&D lines. Our funding constraints mean we cannot hire a dedicated regulatory team for every lab group; instead we must embed small, fixed-cost compliance tasks into existing workflows. We already maintain operational telemetry databases, model versioning pipelines, and incident-response logs for deployed systems; much of Article 12's demand maps onto data we capture but do yet structure or retain at the granularity the regulation requires. Our scientific agenda stays intact; our build-and-deploy process gets stricter guardrails.

proposals.title: Retrofit Logging Middleware Across Active Deployments
proposals.what: We would build a centralized logging middleware layer that injects automatic event capture into our three deployed high-risk systems without rewriting core inference pipelines, targeting the specific data points Article 12(3) mandates for Annex III category 1(a) systems.
proposals.how: A four-engineer team working over two sprints per system would wrap each model's input/output interfaces with log-emitting adapters writing to our existing time-series databases already used for operational monitoring; this is integration, not new procurement.
proposals.why: This converts a compliance obligation into incremental use of infrastructure we have already funded, protecting existing grants from diversion to build logging systems from scratch.

proposals.title: Embed Compliance Gates in the R&D Pipeline
proposals.what: We would restructure our project lifecycle so Article 12 logging specifications become acceptance criteria at the design phase, with each high-risk system proposal requiring a traceability architecture sketch before engineering begins.
proposals.how: Research managers must add a one-page logging specification to every initiation document, reviewed by compliance before model training starts; in-progress projects get a 90-day transition window. This adds two days per cycle but eliminates costly late-stage rework.
proposals.why: Front-loading avoids retrofitting traceability onto architectures never designed for it, protecting both funding timelines and scientific momentum.
